piece.caption:
How to automate Granola and Plaud meeting notes to CRM and project tools using Zapier.

When you record client calls or site meetings on Plaud or Granola, notes usually end up trapped in the app. If nobody copies them into your CRM or task list, agreed pricing and commitments get missed. You can connect Zapier to Claude or ChatGPT as an MCP server. Describe what you want in plain text—like creating Asana tasks for action items or adding meeting summaries to HubSpot deals. Zapier builds the workflow and runs it automatically whenever a new transcript arrives, even when your laptop is off. Zaps use AI only for judgment tasks like summarizing, keeping execution fast and reliable.

How do you currently log client commitments after meetings?

[67] Zapier Blog — 4 ways to automate Granola with your AI agent and Zapier
URL: https://zapier.com/blog/automate-granola
Granola does a great job of capturing your meeting. What happens next is on you: copying the notes into a doc, pasting the recap into Slack, typing the follow-ups into Asana, logging the call in HubSpot. When the meeting ends and the chat window closes, so does the help.
Now you can automate Granola from the AI tool you already use. Install Zapier in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor, describe what should happen to your notes, and your agent builds the automation for you. Zapier runs it from there, long after the chat is closed. Prefer to build in Zapier itself? That works too. Build from wherever you like to work, and the Zap runs the same way.

Granola automations to ask your agent to build
4 ways to automate Granola with Zap templates
Let your agent keep your Granola notes moving
Build automations from wherever you work. Describe the outcome you want, and Zapier connects your tools, runs the steps, and stays on the job after you close the chat. Combine AI with reliable, deterministic automation across 10,000+ apps. Get started for free.
Build Granola automations from your AI assistant
Here's the path from a finished meeting to a finished workflow:
Install Zapier in your AI tool. Add Zapier as a connector or custom MCP server (the connection that lets an AI tool work with Zapier), then connect the apps your notes should reach, like Granola, Google Docs, Slack, and HubSpot. You connect once, and the same connections work from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any AI tool you like.
Describe the job. Say what should happen after a meeting in plain language: "When a new Granola note is ready, save it to a Google Doc and post a short recap in #sales."
Your agent turns it into a Zap. A Zap is an automated workflow that runs on its own. Your agent drafts it, deploys it to Zapier, and shows you what it built.
Zapier runs it. From then on, the Zap starts when a new note lands, whether or not your laptop is open.
Because Zapier connects to 10,000+ apps, the same setup reaches the rest of your stack, too.
You could ask your AI tool to handle your meeting workflows on its own. But building on Zapier gets you a few things chat alone can't:
It starts when something happens. A scheduled task in an AI tool runs at a set time. A Zap can run on a schedule, or it can start when a new Granola note arrives, so the recap goes out right after the meeting and not at 5 p.m.
It reaches your whole stack. Zapier connects to 10,000+ apps so it can do more than built-in connectors. Your agent can log the call on the right HubSpot deal or create a follow-up task in ClickUp, all from the same automation.
It runs the same way every time. The note gets filed, shared, and logged the same way after your 9 a.m. as after your 4 p.m. Zaps use AI only for the steps that need judgment, like pulling out action items, and run everything else as regular steps, which are faster and cheaper.
It fixes itself. If your Google Docs connection expires or a Slack channel gets renamed, your note-sharing Zap shouldn't quietly stop and leave your team without recaps. Zapier logs every run, finds the problem when something breaks, and proposes a fix you can approve, or lets Zapier apply fixes on its own.
Your agent gets access, not your keys. Zapier manages the connections to Granola, your CRM, and your project tools, so you never paste API keys or logins into a chat. Switch from Claude to ChatGPT, or try a new AI tool, and your connections stay put. Everything you build, from any AI tool, shows up in one place in Zapier.
You can just have your agent write a script, and the first version will probably work. But a script needs somewhere to run, a way to hear about new notes, and someone to keep it alive. When an API changes or a login expires, it stops. With Zapier, your agent builds the Zap, Zapier hosts it and runs it from real triggers (a schedule or an app event, like a new Granola note), and keeps your connections working.
Granola automations to ask your agent to build
Not sure where to start? Try one of these prompts in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor with Zapier installed.
Keep notes organized. "When a new Granola note is ready, save it to a Google Doc in my Meeting Notes folder and add a row to my Airtable meeting log."
Share with your team. "After each client call in Granola, post the next steps in the account's Slack channel and email the full note to my team."
Turn notes into tasks. "Read each new Granola note. For every action item assigned to me, create a task in Asana with the meeting name in the title. Skip everything else." This is a good example of a Zap that uses AI only where judgment is needed.
Keep the CRM current. "When a sales call note comes in, find the matching contact in HubSpot, add a three-line summary to the record, and link back to the full note in Granola."
4 ways to automate Granola with Zap templates
Prefer to build in Zapier directly? Zap templates are pre-made Zaps that you set up in Zapier itself. When you click "Try it," the template opens in Zapier, and you can customize it and turn it on from there. Here are four ways to automate Granola with Zap templates. If you'd rather have your agent build a Zap, use the prompts above.
Granola makes it easy to generate clear, reliable notes after every meeting. But if those notes stay in Granola, and you don't make a habit of reviewing them, they can easily get lost. With Zapier, you can automatically route new notes into the tools you already use, like Google Docs or Airtable .
I use an AI notetaker for all my meetings, and while it's great to have a transcript waiting afterward, it can be a little annoying to log in and hunt down the notes each time. I usually end up copying and pasting them into a Google Doc just to keep everything in one place. Automating that step means the notes are already where I expect them to be without me having to do anything.
Whether you prefer a spreadsheet, a shared drive, a Google Doc, or a database, Zapier ensures your notes are automatically sent there, so you can focus on acting on the results of the call instead of copying text.

This way, the team is notified instantly rather than having to search manually through Granola records or waiting for you to send out a recap.

Share recaps. "Post each Plaud summary in #team-updates in Slack. If it came from a customer call, email it to the account owner instead."
